Name: AI-S
Paper Title: AI-Sustainability Discourse Across Social Media: Sentiment, Topics, and Engagement on LinkedIn, X, and Bluesky
Venue Name: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: IJCNLP-AACL 2026
Abstract: We present the first cross-platform computational analysis of AI-sustainability discourse across LinkedIn, X, and Bluesky, using 52,102 posts collected over 15 months. Combining RoBERTa-based sentiment classification with BERTopic topic modeling, we identify 36 topics and compare sentiment, topic distributions, and engagement across platforms. Overall, 43.98% of posts are positive, 40.16% neutral, and 15.86% negative. Sentiment varies by topic rather than by platform: corporate and AI-potential themes are mostly positive, while resource-cost topics carry the highest negative sentiment. Topic distributions differ significantly across platforms: LinkedIn focuses on corporate sustainability, X on hardware and cryptocurrency, and Bluesky on environmental resource costs. Niche topics consistently attract more engagement than high-volume ones. These findings have implications for how organizations and policymakers communicate about AI-sustainability, as topic framing and platform audience composition shape public discourse more than platform selection alone. We release the annotated dataset to support future research.
